Implementation of Mean-Variance & Black-Litterman portfolio optimizations.

#### Description
Implementation of Mean-Variance & Black-Litterman portfolio optimizations using Alglib2 library NLP & QP solvers.

QP solver used for MVO, NLP solver for BL.

#### Related Issue
Closes #1998
Closes #2219

<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->

Python and C# programs can successfully use QuantConnect.Algorithm.Framework library to access portfolio optimization classes. Results between Python and C# implementation are similar.

pr_comments: Currently, the optimization model default value is **null**, and depending on a construction model the optimization algo is set accordinly in the model constructor. That is the only way with optional parameters in C# as they must be a compile time constants, i.e. not objects.

Very close thanks @wildart, I think Alex means: in python the args are:

`self.SetPortfolioConstruction(MeanVarianceOptimizationPortfolioConstructionModel(optimization_method = self.maximum_sharpe_ratio))`

All the other models we've made are "drop-in" compatible as it reduces documentation and difficulty of understanding for the consumers. If possible can you please make it have identical parameter args; so in this case, the python constructor is taking a function passed in from local scope, not a custom class interface+implementation.

`optimization_method = self.maximum_sharpe_ratio`

Where the function takes `returns` and returns `weights`

@AlexCatarino looks like the `opt` is not used; can we remove that from the python version?

More research needed... GPL v2 (http://www.alglib.net/download.php) 

"Despite our best efforts, the FSF has never considered the Apache License to be compatible with GPL version 2, citing the patent termination and indemnification provisions as restrictions not present in the older GPL license. The Apache Software Foundation believes that you should always try to obey the constraints expressed by the copyright holder when redistributing their work."
https://www.apache.org/licenses/GPL-compatibility.html

IANAL but it might mean not even authorized to use for personal use. Will contact AlgLib and see.
@jameschch A solution to licencing issue could be solved by downloading GPL library before building project for personal use. As for commercial purposes you would need a proper license.

I added project conditional building for alglib if the dll is it present in a `Vendor` directory. This would allow to avoid GPL contamination of the project, no GPL code is included, while providing dynamic linking.

> Also, is the SetCovariance method absolutely required? Maybe there's another way we can achieve this, perhaps the optimization method accepts it as an argument? Or since covariance is a pretty standard definition, maybe just a utility function that computes it that all optimizers can invoke to compute it where required.

@mchandschuh Currently `PortfolioConstructionModel` takes optimization method as an object, it would be impossible to create setup the covariance at the construction time. One way of getting around is to pass a type of optimization method to some factory function that would construct a new optimization method object, but then it would be hard to create the optimization method with the specific parameters, like a target return value.

I rebased this PR and added an addition optimization implementations based on Accord Goldfarb-Idnani QP solver. Although Aglib is more precise and stable, you would not have to worry about licencing issues. So right now, default solver is Accord, and if you decided to use in Alglib just put library in `Vendor` folder and recompile. See `Vendor\README.md`.

Any other review issues?

Hey @wildart! On the home stretch! There's been some intense brainstorming on this pull request here at QC HQ. Thank you for your patience as we've been iterating on the final solution. 

 1. Thank you for the Accord optimizer implementation! That is perfect. I spoke with Serge at AlgLib and he disagreed that the linker would avoid GPL contamination, and just for sake of simplicity I agree and think we should just strip it out and use the accord implementation only. We _love_ the implementation and idea -- perhaps its something we can circle back to if Alglib's license changes.

2. Please rebase; we defined a base interface `IPortfolioOptimizer` which should serve both optimizers identified so far. It would be nice if you could please refactor your solution to use it. This also removes the SetCovariance() method -- "the LEAN way" would be to handle it internally so all the optimizers could be directly API Compatible. Hopefully, the python examples should be nice and clear to follow now as they also implement the interface.

We serve a c# and python audience so to minimize the documentation and maximize the ability of people to communicate we aim for the API to be "drop in compatible" meaning they follow _exactly_ the same naming conventions, parameter ordering etc. 

3. Once ready for final PR; please strip out all debug/logging. All our other models are all silent once they're shipped unless there is an error in which case you can make noise :smiley:. 

4. In python we have this method:
```
def WarmUpIndicators(self, history):
    for tuple in history.itertuples():
        self.roc.Update(tuple.Index, tuple.close)
```
But in C# you should use `history.PushThrough` to update your roc indicator. This was a helper we made to make indicators easier.

Alex recommended you start with a new branch and copy your changes manually across. It might help minimize the conflicts.
